A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Omni-Diffusion, and their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison. Retained content can be matched despite pagination changes and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ASR, TTS, visual understanding, image-generation, sampling-step, and qualitative multimodal results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these results and adds original spoken-VQA evaluation, component ablations, DPG-Bench results, and latency measurements.

M1.justification: The reported position-penalty rule changes: v1 specifies a fixed factor of 0.5, whereas v2 specifies a factor decreasing with token index to a minimum of 0.5 (Section 3.4 and Appendix A). The backbone, tokenizers, training objective, training stages, and other inference components remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix B adds DPG-Bench image-generation evaluation and a spoken version of MME using synthesized questions. These extend benchmark coverage within already demonstrated task families; the training datasets in Table 4 and existing evaluation coverage are retained.

E2.justification: The original comparator sets in Tables 1–2 remain unchanged. New Table 7 compares against SD v1.5, SD v2.0, and Show-o. Tables 8–9 additionally introduce latency comparisons against Emu, NExT-GPT, and GLM-4-Voice, previously compared on quality metrics.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands evaluation procedures with measured image-generation time and TTS real-time factor, quantitative MME comparisons across text and synthesized-speech inputs and outputs, DPG-Bench category scores, and component-removal controls. Appendix A also revises the stated position-penalty setting. The PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the sampling-step analysis and inpainting examples, Appendix B.2 adds the first targeted ablations of position penalty and special-token pre-infilling. These test image-generation scores and spoken-response brevity, respectively. Appendix B.4 also extends efficiency analysis to measured latency against autoregressive baselines.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests for its experiments. The new average latency measurements do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the quality scores in Table 3 are retained unchanged, but substantial results are added. These include spoken-input MME-P scores of 1019.9 for text output and 1004.6 for speech output, a DPG-Bench average of 68.20, component-ablation findings, and latency measurements. Table 3 reports 28.57 versus 1.29 seconds for 256 versus 10 text-to-image steps; this is a newly reported step comparison, not a version-to-version performance gain.

T1.justification: The masked-token loss and entropy-based confidence equations remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. The added diffusion-versus-flow discussion is conceptual, and the standard real-time-factor formula serves an empirical timing metric.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: a first any-to-any masked-discrete-diffusion model, joint multimodal token modeling, specialized training and inference techniques, and competitive multimodal performance. The shortened conclusion does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking the new ablations to image quality and avoidance of overly brief spoken responses, and argues for reduced-step efficiency relative to autoregressive baselines. New Appendix C identifies instruction-based visual editing as a future extension through data and model scaling.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly discloses a training batch size of 128 and replaces the fixed position-penalty value with an index-dependent decay description. The batch-size disclosure does not establish a changed training setting. Existing optimizer settings, learning rates, sequence length, dataset quantities, and project-access information are retained.

R1.justification: The positioning against NExT-Omni is substantively revised. v1 describes it as having a text-only backbone and requiring additional generation models; v2 removes that characterization and instead distinguishes flow matching from masked diffusion through training targets and decoding updates. Section 2 also adds CoDi and expands coverage of flow-based and masked-diffusion research, including Fudoki.

P1.justification: v2 makes scattered grammar and terminology corrections, expands related-work explanations, shortens the conclusion, and adds impact and acknowledgment sections. Appendix B becomes an experimental section with subsections, retaining the original image gallery in B.5, followed by a new limitations appendix. The main narrative organization is preserved.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the displayed evidence with spoken-VQA, ablation, DPG-Bench, and latency tables, plus a side-by-side pre-infilling ablation figure. Table 3 gains a latency column and an expanded caption. Earlier image galleries are retained as Figures 9–10 rather than removed or replaced.

improvement.justification: v1 supported spoken visual interaction mainly through examples and efficiency mainly through sampling-step counts, without targeted component ablations. v2 substantially strengthens validation of these central claims through quantitative spoken VQA, measured latency, baseline timing comparisons, and component controls. The improvement concerns supporting evidence rather than higher headline scores. Its strength remains limited by missing timing hardware details, absent uncertainty estimates, and very small numerical effects in the position-penalty ablation.
